content: 1. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Similarly, erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of fosaprepitant through the same mechanism. It is recommended to avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 2. Fosphenytoin decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 3. Gemifloxacin and erythromycin stearate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 4. Gilteritinib and erythromycin stearate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 5. Erythromycin stearate and givinostat both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is unavoidable, obtain ECGs at initiation, during concomitant use, and as clinically indicated. Withhold treatment if the QTc interval exceeds 500 ms or if there is a change from baseline greater than 60 ms. 6. Erythromycin stearate and glasdegib both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for increased risk of QTc prolongation. 7. Granisetron and erythromycin stearate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 8. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 9. Griseofulvin decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 10. Erythromycin stearate and haloperidol both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 11. Erythromycin stearate increases the effects of heparin by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 12. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of hydrocortisone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while hydrocortisone decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate through the same mechanism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 13. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and erythromycin stearate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 14. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of hydroxyprogesterone caproate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 15. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of ibrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor must be used short-term (e.g., for ≤7 days), interrupt ibrutinib therapy until the inhibitor is discontinued. 16. Idelalisib increases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. Idelalisib is a strong CYP3A inhibitor; avoid coadministration with sensitive CYP3A substrates. 17. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of iloperidone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 18. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of imipramine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 19. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of indinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and indinavir increases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate through the same mechanism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 20. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of infigratinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 21. Inotuzumab and erythromycin stearate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is unavoidable, obtain ECGs and monitor electrolytes before and after initiation, and periodically during treatment. 22. Isoflurane and erythromycin stearate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 23. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 24. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 25. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of ivabradine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 26. Ivosidenib and erythromycin stearate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Avoid coadministration of QTc-prolonging drugs with ivosidenib or replace with alternative therapies. Ivosidenib decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor patients for loss of therapeutic effect. 27. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of ixabepilone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 28. Erythromycin stearate and ketoconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 29. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of lapatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and lapatinib increases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate through the same mechanism. This combination is contraindicated. 30. Lasmiditan increases the levels of erythromycin stearate by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 31. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of lemborexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors. 32. Leniolisib increases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inhibiting OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 transporters. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 33. Erythromycin stearate and levoketoconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 34. Lithium and erythromycin stearate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 35. Lofepramine and erythromycin stearate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 36. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of lopinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and lopinavir increases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate through the same mechanism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 37. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of loratadine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 38. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 39. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of lumefantrine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Lumefantrine decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate through the same mechanism. This combination is contraindicated. 40. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of lurbinectedin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 41. Macimorelin and erythromycin stearate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Macimorelin increases the QTc interval by approximately 11 ms. Avoid coadministration with QT-prolonging drugs to reduce the risk of torsade de pointes. Allow sufficient washout time of QT-prolonging drugs before administering macimorelin. 42. Maprotiline and erythromycin stearate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 43. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 44. Marijuana increases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 45. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of mestranol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 46. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of methadone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 47. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of methylprednisolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while methylprednisolone decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate through the same mechanism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 48. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 49. Miconazole vaginal increases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 50. Erythromycin stearate decreases the effects of microbiota oral therapy through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. Complete antibiotic regimens 2–4 days before initiating microbiota oral therapy. 51. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of midazolam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 52. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of midazolam intranasal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. Coadministration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors increases systemic exposure to midazolam, potentially prolonging sedation. 53. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 54. Mirtazapine and erythromycin stearate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 55. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of mizolastine by decreasing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 56. Erythromycin stearate and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 57. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 58. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of naloxegol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 59. Nefazodone increases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 60. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of nelfinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate through the same mechanism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 61. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of neratinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 62. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 63. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of nicardipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 64. Nifedipine increases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 65. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of nilotinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and nilotinib increases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate through the same mechanism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. This combination is contraindicated. 66. Nilutamide increases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 67. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of nirogacestat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 68. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of nisoldipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 69. Nortriptyline and erythromycin stearate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 70. Erythromycin stearate and octreotide both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 71. Olanzapine and erythromycin stearate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 72. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of olaparib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration with moderate CYP3A inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the olaparib dose to 200 mg (capsule) or 150 mg (tablet) twice daily. Do not substitute tablets with capsules. 73. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of omaveloxolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If unavoidable, reduce the omaveloxolone dose to 100 mg/day and monitor closely for adverse effects. If adverse effects emerge, further reduce the dose to 50 mg/day. 74. Erythromycin stearate and ondansetron both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Avoid in patients with congenital long QT syndrome. ECG monitoring is recommended with concomitant medications that prolong the QT interval, electrolyte abnormalities, CHF, or bradyarrhythmias. 75. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of osimertinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If no alternative treatment exists, monitor the patient closely for adverse effects. 76. Oxaliplatin and erythromycin stearate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 77. Oxcarbazepine decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs.
